records.title: A 3D-Printed Biochemical-Mechano-Thermally Responsive Multicellular Tumor Organoid Platform Decodes Biochemical-Physical Regulation of Cancer-Immune Crosstalk and Chemoresistance.
records.abstract: Oral tumors are not shaped by biochemical signals alone; they also evolve within mechanically active and thermally fluctuating microenvironments that critically regulate malignant progression, immune remodeling, and therapeutic resistance. Here, we develop a dynamic bioorthogonal organoid platform that couples a 3D-printed photothermal elastic scaffold with an interpenetrating hydrogel network derived from decellularized oral mucosa extracellular matrix, enabling the reconstruction of in vivo-like structural support, matrix-derived biochemical cues, spatial cellular compartmentalization, and dynamic physical stimulation. Through click chemistry-mediated cell anchorage and hydrogel encapsulation, oral cancer cells and macrophages are spatially organized into a compartmentalized cancer-immune niche. Under cyclic mechanical stretch and near-infrared-triggered periodic photothermal stimulation, dynamic culture markedly enhances cancer cell proliferation and glycolytic reprogramming while concomitantly polarizing macrophages toward a pro-tumoral M2 phenotype. In both monoculture and coculture settings, biochemical-mechano-thermal stimulation substantially increases cancer cell chemoresistance. Mechanistically, these biochemical-physical cues activate stress-adaptive and survival programs while enriching cancer stem-like populations. In a xenograft mouse model exposed to in vivo biochemical, mechanical and thermal stimulation, dynamic conditioning markedly accelerates tumor progression, enhances metastatic potential, and confers pronounced chemoresistance. Together, this study establishes a biomimetic multicellular tumor platform for uncovering how dynamic biochemical-physical cues orchestrate cancer-immune crosstalk and therapeutic failure.

records.title: Linking preclinical models with functional imaging and artificial intelligence to decode tumor angiogenesis.
records.abstract: Tumor angiogenesis is a hallmark of cancer, influencing oxygen delivery, immune cell trafficking, and therapeutic response. Although anti-angiogenic therapies have achieved clinical relevance, their efficacy remains limited by tumor heterogeneity, adaptive resistance, and insufficient functional assessment of tumor vasculature. In this review, we evaluate preclinical models of tumor angiogenesis with a focus on their ability to generate quantitative and physiologically relevant readouts. We discuss established assays such as tube formation, fibrin bead assay, aortic ring, and chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) models, alongside emerging systems including vascularized organoids and organ-on-a-chip platforms, as well as zebrafish and murine tumor models. Particular emphasis is placed on advanced imaging modalities enabling longitudinal assessment of perfusion, permeability, and vascular remodeling, as well as on the growing role of artificial intelligence (AI) in automated and quantitative data interpretation. We further highlight the integration of single-cell and multi-omics approaches for resolving endothelial heterogeneity and tumor-stroma interactions. By linking biologically relevant models with functional imaging and computational analysis, this review outlines strategies to improve the predictive power and translational relevance of angiogenesis research.

records.title: Tissues as a synthetic target - a framework for the multiscale molecular design of thermogelling polymers.
records.abstract: Tissues are living, water-swollen composite polymer networks whose dynamic biochemical composition, hierarchical architecture, and mechanics collectively regulate cell behavior and physiological function. Recreating these properties across biological and biomedical contexts (e.g., 2D and 3D cell culture, tissue engineering, organoid culture, and regenerative medicine) remains a critical challenge as existing synthetic matrices cannot fully recapitulate the multiscale organization and dynamic properties of native extracellular matrices. Most hydrogel platforms rely on "drag-n-drop" combinations of polymers, crosslinkers, fabrication methods, and bioactive motifs to approximate the biophysical and biochemical properties of an individual tissue or biomedical context. In this Review, we seek to motivate the pursuit of thermogel-based "plug-n-play" approaches by framing tissues as synthetic targets and examining the potential of polymers that undergo thermally-triggered assembly to serve as modular building blocks for next-generation synthetic ECMs. The ultimate goal is a universal framework for programming composition, structure, mechanics, and biofunction from a common multiscale molecular design language. We first closely examine the composition, assembly, and properties of ECMs to clearly establish targets of interest and processes that may serve as inspiration. Finally, we connect the thermodynamic principles of lower critical solution temperature behavior with macromolecular topology, phase separation, and hierarchical assembly to establish design opportunities for creating thermogelling polymers that more closely mimic the fibrous, hydrated, mechanically adaptive, and cell-instructive nature of native ECMs. We propose that future progress will require the integration of precise polymer synthesis, topology-dictated assembly, macromolecular crowding, high-throughput formulation, and multiscale characterization to establish predictive structure-assembly-property relationships. This framework is intended to facilitate the transition of thermogelling polymers from injectable or temperature-responsive materials to a latent scalable synthetic platform for writing bespoke tissue-like microenvironments from molecularly programmed building blocks.

records.title: Paracrine Bone-Derived Senescent Secretome is Associated with Spatially Patterned ECM Remodeling and Altered Biomechanics in Human Brain Organoids.
records.abstract: Aging is increasingly recognized as a systemic process, yet the mechanisms by which signals from senescent peripheral cells accelerate brain aging remain poorly defined. Here, we used chronic exposure of human cerebral organoids to the secretome of senescent osteocytes to investigate how peripheral aging signals from bone reshape brain tissue architecture. We combined spatially resolved optical fiber-based interferometry nanoindentation with transcriptomic and immunofluorescence profiling, revealing distinct mechanical features across complementary measurements, including lower apparent modulus in intact organoids and spatially localized regions of elevated modulus in cryosectioned specimens. This spatially heterogeneous biomechanical remodeling was accompanied by upregulation of extracellular matrix, inflammatory, and senescence pathways, and suppression of neurodevelopmental and synaptic gene networks. Our results suggest that chronic paracrine exposure to senescent osteocyte-derived secretome is associated with localized extracellular matrix-related remodeling and mechanical vulnerability in human brain tissue, providing insight into how peripheral cellular senescence may contribute to regional brain fragility during aging. These pilot-scale findings were obtained using a single iPSC line and a single conditioned-medium batch, with one to six experimental replicates per condition across assays; the mechanical analyses were exploratory.

records.title: Advanced In Vitro Platforms for Experimental Liver Research: From Organoids and Liver-on-Chip to Omics and Artificial Intelligence.
records.abstract: Hepatocytes perform essential physiological functions in the human body. Gaining more profound insight into the liver structure, diseases, and physiology by using in vitro models can help to propose more relevant clinical applications. Conventional in vitro liver models, such as two-dimensional (2D) cell cultures, fail to adequately replicate the hepatic microenvironment, even when improved by adding additional cell types and extracellular matrix (ECM). These models do not address all necessary key components to mimic in vivo conditions, particularly multicellularity, specific ECM, and proper biophysical and biochemical parameters. Organoids, 3D-bioprinted constructs, and liver-on-chip platforms establish physiologically relevant models by improving cell-cell and cell-matrix interactions and multicellular architecture. For a comprehensive understanding of the liver's interconnections with related tissues and organs, a multi-organ-on-chip is a useful platform for more systemic studies. Also, other interdisciplinary approaches, particularly omics and artificial intelligence (AI), can enhance the accuracy of experimental and pre-clinical data achieved by such advanced in vitro liver platforms. This review highlights developing platforms for integrated approaches in experimental liver studies to enable researchers to have a holistic view of the liver in physiologic and pathologic conditions.

records.title: CD147+ Cancer-Associated Fibroblasts Promote PD-L1 Expression in Hepatocellular Carcinoma via TIMP2/MMP2/IL-6 Signaling.
records.abstract: Targeting CD147 on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells has demonstrated therapeutic efficacy. Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) have been identified as critical components of the tumor microenvironment. The role of CD147 in CAFs is still unclear, and this study aims to explore its function. We analyzed single-cell RNA-seq data to identify CD147 expression in CAFs. Flow cytometry and multiplex immunohistochemistry (mIHC) were used to validate protein levels. CD147 function was assessed via shRNA/overexpression. Protein interactions were examined by molecular docking and co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP). Organoid co-culture system was established to study tumor-immune interactions. Single-cell sequencing and mIHC analyses have confirmed the presence of CD147+CAFs within tumor and adjacent tissues, with tumor-derived CAFs exhibiting elevated CD147 transcript levels. The proportion of CD147+ CAFs varied among patients and demonstrated no significant correlation with CD147 expression in HCC cells. Functionally, CD147+ CAFs secreted higher levels of IL-6 compared to CD147- counterparts. We elucidated a mechanism wherein CD147 on CAFs competitively binds to the tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinase 2 (TIMP2), thereby diminishing TIMP2-mediated inhibition of matrix metalloproteinase 2 (MMP2). Free MMP2 enhances IL-6 secretion via the integrin α5β1 signaling pathway. IL-6 subsequently upregulates PD-L1 expression on HCC cells. This phenomenon was validated both in vitro and organoid co-culture model, where a higher burden of CD147+ CAFs correlated with increased levels of IL-6 and PD-L1. Our study delineates a novel CAF-driven immunosuppressive pathway in HCC, where CD147+ CAFs enhance tumor cell PD-L1 expression and susceptibility to immune checkpoint blockade via a TIMP2/MMP2/IL-6 axis. CD147 has been primarily viewed as a therapeutic marker on HCC cells and has supported the development of CD147-targeted treatment strategies. This study shows that CD147 is also expressed in CAFs and functions as an independent regulator of the immune microenvironment by promoting IL 6 secretion and tumor PD-L1 upregulation. Importantly, CD147 expression in CAFs is not correlated with its expression in tumor cells. These findings suggest that evaluation of CD147 in both tumor and stromal compartments may improve patient stratification and may identify additional patients who could potentially benefit from CD147-targeted or combination immunotherapy approaches.

records.title: Benchmarking biological knowledge-graph priors against single-cell foundation models for Perturb-seq prediction.
records.abstract: Perturb-seq prediction increasingly relies on either biological graph priors or single-cell foundation models, but their relative value is difficult to interpret when architectures, split definitions and graph sources vary simultaneously. We benchmarked STRING functional associations and Gene Ontology co-annotation against dense, self-edge-only and exact-degree-rewired supports in one fixed graph-attention backbone, with a separate 200-HVG STRING-GO-control-co-expression sensitivity. Four public Perturb-seq datasets, three nested gene-space scales and three optimisation seeds were evaluated on held-out guide conditions; GEARS, scGPT and Geneformer were evaluated on the same held-out conditions, output-gene panels and Pearson-r metric after model-specific validity checks. At 200 highly variable genes, STRING-GO improved the equal-dataset Pearson r by +0.016 (95% interval [+0.010, +0.022]) relative to dense support. Dataset effects were positive in Adamson (+0.017), Norman (+0.015), Replogle K562 (+0.017) and Replogle RPE1 (+0.014), and 122/200 guide conditions improved (0.61 [0.54,0.68]). The top-20-gene Jaccard difference was +0.009 [+0.006,+0.012]. STRING-GO exceeded self-edge-only support by +0.024 [+0.018,+0.029] and the mean of ten exact-degree rewires by +0.011 [+0.005,+0.017]. The native-panel effect declined from +0.016 at 200 genes to +0.009 at 1000 genes; the 1000-200 interaction was -0.006 [-0.011,-0.002]. The primary graph-support comparison was formulated and conducted during peer-review revision rather than planned as an a priori confirmatory study. All three external models passed implementation-specific checks. Across 36 protocol-matched dataset-scale contrasts, 32 were within the descriptive ±0.030 reference envelope and four were outside, all favouring the external model. These results demonstrate a modest empirical predictive improvement under the evaluated matched protocol; they do not by themselves establish practical biological relevance.

records.title: AI-enabled fungal biomanufacturing: from genome mining to the artificial intelligence virtual cell.
records.abstract: Fungi are important chassis organisms for sustainable biomanufacturing owing to their strong secretion capacity, metabolic diversity, and adaptability to industrial processes. Driven by the rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI), computational approaches that enable machines to learn patterns from data and make predictions, together with omics technologies and synthetic biology, data- and model-driven strategies are increasingly reshaping fungal cell factory design and optimization. This review summarizes recent advances in AI-enabled fungal biomanufacturing, covering AI-assisted genome mining, enzyme and pathway analysis, genome editing, metabolic network modeling, and intelligent fermentation control. The review further highlights the emerging concept of the artificial intelligence virtual cell (AIVC), which integrates multi-omics data, mechanistic modeling, and machine learning-based approaches into a unified multiscale framework for simulating dynamic cellular behaviors. The technical foundations and potential applications of AIVC in fungal metabolic engineering, drug discovery, agriculture, and environmental biotechnology are reviewed. Finally, key challenges-data quality and standardization, cross-scale model integration and interpretability, and the gap between in silico prediction and experimental validation-are highlighted. This review provides a systematic perspective on the role of AI and virtual cell technologies in advancing next generation fungal biotechnology.

records.title: PHAROS: turning single-cell perturbation models into target-directed drug-combination screens.
records.abstract: Combination therapies are central to cancer treatment, but exhaustive screening is impractical. We introduce PHAROS, a framework that turns a pretrained single-cell perturbation model into a target-directed search engine for drug combinations. PHAROS predicts how a cell population changes under a drug, one drug at a time, then chains these predictions together to simulate drug combinations. It scores each simulated outcome against the desired target state and uses a search algorithm to find the most promising combinations, all without retraining the underlying model. Across two independent combinatorial perturbation datasets, PHAROS recovered exact or mechanism-matched two-drug responses in cell lines, both seen and unseen during model training. Its rankings were specific to the requested conversion and were not explained by single-drug effects, additive effects, or shared mechanism of action. In exploratory analyses of patient-derived metastatic HR+/HER2- breast tumors and basal cell carcinoma (BCC), PHAROS prioritized FDA-approved regimens, distinguished combinations by their predicted tumor-versus-immune objective profiles, and nominated pathway-level hypotheses, while explicitly identifying both tumor cohorts as outside the model's supported distribution. PHAROS provides a modular route from pretrained virtual-cell models to inverse, single-cell combination-screening platforms.

records.title: Pop-Corn: Predicting Perturbation Phenotype Effects Across Single-Cell and Spatial Contexts.
records.abstract: Genetic perturbations can reshape cell populations by altering the relative abundance of specific cell types and states within the profiled population, including increases, decreases and states that become detectable after perturbation. Pooled single-cell screens, such as Perturb-seq, measure such responses at scale. However, only a small fraction of possible perturbations can be tested experimentally. A central challenge is therefore to predict compositional shifts induced by unseen perturbations. Many perturbation-prediction methods do not directly optimize for this outcome; instead, they predict gene-expression responses and infer cell-type and cell-state composition downstream. Surprisingly, we find that even models that accurately predict perturbation-induced changes in average gene expression perform poorly at forecasting these compositional shifts. To address this gap, we present Pop-Corn, a method that directly predicts how a perturbation reshapes cell-type composition without reconstructing gene expression. In the primary T-cell benchmark, Pop-Corn predicted the overall cell-state composition of held-out perturbations more accurately than the evaluated expression-prediction pipelines, while better preserving the diversity of observed cell states. We further extend Pop-Corn to intact tissue, where it predicts perturbation-induced cell-type proportion changes in local cellular neighborhoods and uses attention patterns to generate hypotheses about context-dependent cellular interactions. Retrospective virtual screens support the use of Pop-Corn to prioritize perturbations for experimental follow-up according to their predicted effects on cell-state composition.

records.title: Integrated computation-guided thermostabilization of the fungal sweet protein Honey Truffle Sweetener.
records.abstract: Thermostability limits the use of sweet proteins as sugar substitutes in thermally processed foods. Here, we report an integrated computation-guided workflow for thermostabilizing Honey Truffle Sweetener (HTS), a recently identified fungal sweet protein with low intrinsic stability. We determined the HTS crystal structure and used it to guide subsequent computational analyses. Rosetta and ThermoMPNN evaluated candidate substitutions from complementary physics-based and deep-learning-based perspectives, and the selected single-mutant library was experimentally characterized. The resulting melting-temperature data were then used to develop SMRC-Net, which combines mutation-centered features from the ESM2 protein language model with molecular dynamics-derived structural descriptors to support mutation prioritization. Repeated nested cross-validation supported quantitative Tm prediction within the HTS scaffold, while prospective testing showed 9/10 directional agreement in a small, computationally selected variant set. Validated substitutions were then assembled stepwise in small modules, followed by the introduction of an engineered disulfide bond. The final variant, FM, had a melting temperature of 82.1 °C, 27.5 °C higher than that of wild-type HTS. Untreated FM retained sweetness, while separate heat- and pH-treatment assays showed retained solubility and largely preserved secondary-structure profiles. Sweetness after these treatments was not evaluated. Molecular dynamics analyses indicated that FM was not uniformly rigidified but instead exhibited localized flexibility redistribution and a more consolidated conformational ensemble. This work provides a practical computation-guided framework for protein thermostabilization, with potential applicability to other compact proteins.

records.title: Design-Evolution Synergy Enables New-to-Nature Enzyme Chemistry.
records.abstract: Directed evolution and machine-learning-assisted evolution have transformed biocatalysis by enabling rapid optimisation of catalytic performance within compatible protein scaffolds. In parallel, advances in deep-learning-driven de novo protein design have expanded accessible protein architectural space, enabling the generation of functional catalysts for increasingly challenging transformations. We herein report a synergistic design-evolution strategy to encode new-to-nature regio- and enantioselective C-H amination reactions using engineered de novo haemproteins to synthesise chiral piperidines, a privileged pharmacophore in drug discovery. By integrating motif scaffolding, computational re-design, and directed evolution, we demonstrate de novo enzyme design can enable challenging, high-energy-barrier enzyme chemistry with programmable regio- and enantioselectivity, high catalytic efficiency, excellent enzyme stability, and scaffold diversity.

records.title: RNASeek: A Cross-Phyla Generative Foundation Model for Multipurpose RNA Modeling and Reinforcement Learning-Based Design.
records.abstract: RNA plays central roles in regulating information flow and provides a versatile substrate for engineering biological functions. While large language models (LLMs) have transformed natural language processing and protein design, a general framework connecting RNA foundation models to functional sequence design remains limited. Here, we present RNASeek, a 1.6-billion-parameter generative foundation model built on a DeepSeek architecture and trained on a cross-phyla transcriptomic corpus for RNA sequence representation and generation. Natural-language tokens enable flexible conditional prediction and sequence design using a unified backbone. RNASeek captures species-specific transcript features and intron-exon boundaries in a zero-shot setting. We then fine-tune RNASeek to predict ribozyme self-cleavage activity and viral mRNA stability, revealing interpretable sequence features associated with function, including ribozyme loop flexibility and stem stability, as well as AU-rich motifs associated with mRNA stability. We use these functional predictors as reward models and apply Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to update RNASeek's generation policy toward sequences with desired properties. GRPO-guided generation produces faster-cleaving ribozymes and stability-enhancing 3' UTRs while satisfying user-specified IUPAC constraints. Experimentally validated RNASeek-generated ribozymes achieve wild-type levels of activity, while RNASeek-generated 3' UTR sequences exceed the performance of the training data and benchmarked AI-generated 3' UTRs. Together, RNASeek establishes a unified pretrain-predict-optimize framework that connects learned RNA function to controllable de novo sequence design and provides a general strategy for engineering regulatory RNAs with desired properties.

records.title: Correction: From atoms to fragments: a coarse representation for efficient and functional protein design.
3D CNN-CVAE and LSTM-guided de novo design of rotigotine derivatives targeting dopamine D1 and D3 receptors in restless legs syndrome.
records.abstract: Restless legs syndrome (RLS) is a chronic neurological disorder associated with altered dopaminergic signaling, while long-term dopamine agonist therapy may be limited by augmentation and reduced clinical benefit. This study applied a three-dimensional convolutional neural network conditional variational autoencoder integrated with long short-term memory molecular generation to design rotigotine-derived candidates targeting dopamine D1 and D3 receptors. Fourteen unique derivatives were generated and screened through pocket prediction, molecular docking, interaction profiling, pharmacophore analysis, density functional theory, ADMET prediction, 500 ns molecular dynamics simulations performed in explicit water without a lipid bilayer, and MM/GBSA calculations. Docking protocol validation using DockRMSD yielded RMSD values of 1.009 Å for Mevidalen in the D1 receptor and 1.359 Å for PD-128907 in the D3 receptor, supporting acceptable reproduction of both experimental binding poses. In docking-based ranking, AI Derivative 1 was placed above rotigotine for D1 (-5.744 vs -5.629 kcal/mol) and D3 (-7.934 vs -7.288 kcal/mol) and formed additional hydrogen-bond and hydrophobic contacts; the D1 difference of approximately 0.1 kcal/mol lies within the intrinsic uncertainty of docking scoring functions and is not interpreted as evidence of improved affinity. Docking scores are used throughout as ranking and prioritization metrics rather than quantitative binding free energies. It also exhibited a smaller HOMO-LUMO gap, a higher predicted LD50, and a shift from toxicity class 3 to class 4. Molecular dynamics analyses, including RMSD, RMSF, radius of gyration, solvent-accessible surface area, hydrogen bonding, DCCM, PCA, and free-energy landscapes, are reported as descriptive observations from single non-membrane trajectories and are not used to claim physiological relevance or superior binding stability. MM/GBSA estimates were favorable under the applied computational conditions. AI Derivative 1 therefore represents a computationally prioritized lead requiring experimental validation.

records.title: Integrative Approaches in Protein Structure/Function Analysis, Design, and Engineering.
records.abstract: Over the past decade, protein design has drawn considerable attention and emerged as a promising tool for sustainable and efficient biocatalytic processes, driven by breakthroughs in DNA sequencing, gene synthesis, bioinformatics, and artificial intelligence. Enabled by strategies such as directed evolution, structure/function analysis, and (semi-)rational design, engineered enzymes can now accommodate nonnatural substrates, catalyze novel reactions, and operate under harsh conditions including elevated temperatures and organic solvents.This chapter provides a comprehensive overview of major strategies in protein design including directed evolution, rational design, and semi-rational design. Emphasis is placed on recent advances in high-throughput screening technologies, identification of functionally critical residues, and optimization of site-specific mutations. Furthermore, the integration of artificial intelligence and multiscale modeling to enzyme design is discussed, highlighting data-driven decision-making and deep learning-assisted prediction of enzymatic performance. Looking forward, biocatalysis is poised to further expand its applications in valorization of renewable resources, biofuels, and synthetic chemistry. Powered by ongoing advances in AI and computational protein design, the development of enzymes with unprecedented catalytic functions is anticipated to accelerate rapidly.

records.title: Real-World HRR Testing Pathways and Patterns of Detected Alterations in Prostate Cancer From the Multinational ARON-3 Study.
records.abstract: Homologous recombination repair (HRR) testing is increasingly relevant in prostate cancer because it identifies patients who may benefit from biomarker-guided treatment strategies, including poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPi). However, real-world implementation of HRR testing remains variable across countries and clinical settings, and the extent to which current testing pathways capture actionable alterations is not well defined. ARON-3 is a multinational, multicentre, retrospective real-world study of patients with prostate cancer. In this subanalysis, we assessed genomic testing uptake within the overall ARON-3 cohort and characterised HRR testing pathways and detected pathogenic alterations among patients with available genomic results. Genomic testing included germline, somatic tumour, and/or circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) assays performed in routine practice across participating centres. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify clinicopathologic factors associated with undergoing genomic HRR testing. Among 2,192 patients included in ARON-3, genomic testing results were available for 719 (33%). Among tested patients, 660 (92%) underwent germline testing and 610 (85%) somatic testing; 549 (77%) underwent both, whereas 109 (15%) had germline-only and 61 (8%) somatic-only testing. In multivariable analysis, metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, high-volume disease, and Gleason score > 8 were independently associated with higher odds of testing, while age ≥ 70 years was associated with lower odds of testing. Overall, 238 tested patients (33%) harboured pathogenic HRR alterations, corresponding to 11% of the entire ARON-3 cohort. Somatic pathogenic alterations were more frequent than germline alterations. BRCA2 was the most frequently altered gene, while non-BRCA1/2 alterations were also detected, particularly in centres using broader multigene panels. Most centres relied on BRCA1/2-focused assays, and the use of liquid biopsy remained limited. This multinational real-world analysis demonstrates substantial heterogeneity in HRR testing uptake and testing pathways across participating ARON-3 centres. Testing was more commonly performed in patients with more advanced disease features, suggesting that clinically relevant subgroups may still be differentially selected for genomic assessment. Broader and more standardised implementation of comprehensive HRR profiling may improve the identification of actionable alterations and strengthen precision medicine in prostate cancer.

records.title: Advances in peptidomics: analytical strategies and biological insights for clinical applications.
records.abstract: Endogenous peptides are emerging as key regulators of physiological and pathological processes and represent promising biomarkers and therapeutic targets. Advances in peptidomics have substantially improved their discovery and characterization, providing new insights into peptide biogenesis, biological functions, and clinical applications. This review summarizes current knowledge on endogenous peptide generation, analytical workflows, biological functions, and emerging diagnostic and therapeutic applications. A literature search was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science, focusing primarily on studies published between 2020 and 2026. This review: (1) examines MS-based analytical strategies for peptidome characterization; (2) highlights major peptidomics subfields, including immunopeptidomics, neuropeptidomics, degradomics, fragmentomics, and secretomics; (3) discusses current biological and clinical applications, with emphasis on biomarker discovery, disease monitoring, and theranostic development in oncology, neurodegenerative, metabolic, reproductive, and infectious diseases. The review also summarizes current advances in liquid biopsy peptidomics. Peptidomics is evolving from a discovery-driven discipline into a clinically relevant platform for biomarker identification and therapeutic development. Future progress will depend on standardized workflows, advanced MS technologies, AI-supported data analysis, and multi-omics integration to enable robust clinical translation and precision medicine.

records.title: [Urinary biomarkers: A promising tool for modern nephrology].
records.abstract: To avoid the need for renal biopsy, which remains an invasive procedure, numerous urinary biomarkers have been investigated for the detection, risk stratification, and prediction of disease progression in patients with acute or chronic kidney disease. Often referred to as a form of "liquid biopsy," some of these molecular candidates, particularly proteins and peptides, have shown considerable robustness and clinical potential. This review outlines the concept of a biomarker and the key stages involved in its development, drawing on practical examples such as prognostic signatures for antenatal renal developmental abnormalities and the prediction of acute kidney injury, as well as diagnostic applications in common clinical settings, including glomerular diseases using urinary soluble CD163 and acute interstitial nephritis using CXCL9. Methods used for biomarker measurement are also discussed. Despite encouraging results, even the most advanced biomarkers have struggled to progress beyond external multicenter validation because of methodological challenges related to both the underlying technologies and the heterogeneity of patient cohorts. As of 2026, these biomarkers remain primarily research tools, and a broad consensus on their routine clinical use has yet to emerge.

records.title: Micro/Nanostructured Materials and Microfluidic Diagnostic Platforms Enable Multimodal Detection of Circulating Tumor Cells.
records.abstract: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs), as pivotal targets in liquid biopsy, offer dynamic, multidimensional insights into tumor heterogeneity and metastatic progression. However, their extreme rarity, pronounced heterogeneity, and the complexity of the blood microenvironment severely constrain detection accuracy. Advances in micro/nanomaterials and functional device engineering have enabled substantial improvements in CTC enrichment efficiency by refining the topographical and chemical properties of capture interfaces. These innovations also provide a compatible foundation for multimodal molecular profiling. This review systematically outlines the structure-function relationships of functionalized nanomaterials, microfiltration substrates, and biomimetic microfluidic devices, highlighting how material parameters-such as nanoscale architectures and membrane pore sizes-govern CTC capture performance. We further explore the integration of micro/nanomaterials with functional platforms for multidimensional molecular analyses across DNA, RNA, and protein levels. Coupled with emerging digital PCR technologies, these systems show promise in overcoming the sensitivity barriers associated with rare mutation detection and protein quantification, enabling multi-omics data fusion. We also discuss how artificial intelligence (AI)-driven feature selection, clustering, and prediction integrate multidimensional data to decode tumor heterogeneity and guide disease monitoring. Despite rapid progress, key challenges remain-including the lack of standardization, limited integration of multi-omic datasets, and the need for robust clinical validation. Future directions may lie in the convergence of microfluidic-integrated materials, single-cell multi-omics, and AI-driven analytics to establish dynamic, high-resolution monitoring platforms that bridge the gap between fundamental research and clinical precision oncology.

records.title: Prognostic biomarkers in non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer: biological basis and evidence.
records.abstract: To review prognostic and treatment-response biomarkers for non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC), with particular attention to biological function, specimen type, assay method, statistical evidence, and possible clinical use. We conducted a focused narrative search of PubMed, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library for English-language human studies published from January 2015 to August 2026, supplemented by earlier pivotal studies and reference-list screening. Priority was given to NMIBC cohorts reporting recurrence, progression, survival, or response to intravesical therapy. We considered cohort specificity, sample size, multivariable analysis, testing in an independent population, and assay standardisation. Tumour-tissue markers such as stromal antigen 2 (STAG2), fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3), fibroblast activation protein-α, the urokinase plasminogen activator system, and cadherins are linked to chromosomal stability, growth-factor signalling, stromal remodelling, extracellular-matrix invasion, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. Urinary RNAs and plasma circulating tumour DNA permit non-invasive sampling, although results depend on specimen handling and assay conditions. Blood-derived inflammatory indices are inexpensive but non-specific. Most evidence comes from retrospective single-cohort studies; reported effects and cut-offs are not always consistent, and few markers materially improve clinicopathological models. None of the biomarkers reviewed can currently replace guideline-based risk stratification or cystoscopic surveillance. Future studies should define assays and thresholds prospectively, test them in independent cohorts, and show that adding a biomarker improves prediction and patient management at an acceptable cost.

records.title: Identifying Differentially Expressed Proteins via Plasma Exosomal Proteomics.
records.abstract: Extracellular vesicle (EV) proteomics can be used to study intercellular communication and find biomarkers of non-invasive diseases. Traditional separation methods (ultracentrifugation, size exclusion chromatography) and data-dependent acquisition (DDA) mass spectrometry usually have the drawbacks of copurification of pollutants, poor reproducibility, and insufficient sampling of low-abundance peptides. This protocol describes a workflow for label-free extracellular vesicle proteomics, which combines size exclusion chromatography for vesicle separation, data-independent acquisition (DIA) for deep discovery, and parallel reaction monitoring (PRM) for targeted verification. Plasma-derived extracellular vesicles are treated by standardized lysis, digestion, and LC-MS/MS procedures, so that the protein group of extracellular vesicles can be identified and quantified robustly. The main advantages of this scheme are that it can achieve high quantitative reproducibility, unbiased detection of low-intensity peptides, and seamless transition from discovery to targeted verification, while also being suitable for liquid biopsy samples and various cardiovascular diseases. Key features • Combines size exclusion chromatography (SEC)-based EV isolation with label-free data-independent acquisition (DIA) for deep, unbiased discovery-phase extracellular vesicle proteomics. • Employs parallel reaction monitoring (PRM) for orthogonal, highly sensitive targeted validation of candidate biomarkers discovered by DIA. • PRM records the entire, high-resolution fragment ion spectrum for the targeted peptide. • Developed for atrial fibrillation; adaptable to other cardiovascular diseases, therapy monitoring, and liquid biopsies.
